items.stem: Why can referencing window directly in a component's setup break a Nuxt universal app?

options.text: setup runs on the server during SSR, where window is undefined
options.rationale: Correct: server rendering has no browser globals; guard with onMounted or import.meta.client.

options.text: window is reserved by Nuxt and cannot be used anywhere
options.rationale: window is fine in client-only contexts.

options.text: Nuxt forbids all browser APIs permanently
options.rationale: Browser APIs work on the client; only SSR lacks them.

options.text: window only works inside Pinia stores
options.rationale: Pinia does not change the availability of window.

items.explanation: Correct: server rendering has no browser globals; guard with onMounted or import.meta.client.

items.stem: Which TWO are correct about runtimeConfig in Nuxt? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Values under the public key are exposed to the client
options.rationale: Correct: public config is intentionally shipped to the browser.

options.text: Private top-level config is available only on the server
All runtimeConfig values are always sent to the client
options.rationale: Only public values are; sending private ones would leak secrets.

options.text: runtimeConfig cannot be overridden by environment variables
options.rationale: It is designed to be overridden by env vars at runtime.

items.explanation: Correct: public config is intentionally shipped to the browser.

items.stem: A developer stores per-request user data in a module-level variable in a Nuxt server route. What is the risk?

options.text: State can leak across concurrent requests and between users on the server
options.rationale: Correct: module scope is shared on the server, so request data can bleed across users.

options.text: Nothing; module variables are per-request by default
options.rationale: Module variables are shared, not per-request.
The risk is specifically on the shared server runtime.

options.text: It improves performance with no downside
options.rationale: The correctness and security risk outweighs any perceived gain.

items.explanation: Correct: module scope is shared on the server, so request data can bleed across users.
